Of 176 items, **14 actually hold a lane**. The other 162 are either self-healing, dead pointers, or a genuine queue for your judgement.

## What changed while I built it

The three dead janitors are fixed and **all 12 stale claims behind them are swept**:

- **hitbut** [#108](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/108) → reclaimed 22:07:35
- **ClaudiniteWebsite** [#239](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/issues/239)–[#262](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/issues/262), 7 items → 22:08:58–22:09:11 (some ~34h old)
- **GoogleCalendarEventCreator** [#979](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/979), [#980](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/980), [#1036](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/1036), [#1038](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/1038) → 22:09:15–22:09:22 (~41h old)

Zero `task:agent` left in any of the three. **Rule B is now confirmed working end-to-end**, watched live rather than inferred.

## Two corrections worth your attention

**My first fix was wrong, and the engine caught it.** I re-labelled the three parked janitor items `task:ready`; all three closed `task:obsolete` instead of running. Their bodies point at `packs/basics/tasks/task-janitor/` — the **pre-migration path** — so the executor correctly retired them as stale pointers. The engine also refuses a hand-made item for a scheduled task outright. The sanctioned lever turned out to be the scheduler's **`wake` input**, which mints a fresh standing item; that's what actually worked.

**The migration left a fleet-wide trap.** Every work item filed before the move still names `basics/task-janitor`. They don't fail loudly — they retire as `obsolete`, which reads like "nothing to do". [MissingBulbWebsite #219](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/issues/219) did exactly this at 14:00 today and I initially misread it as a clean no-op. Any repo whose janitor item predates the migration will silently skip its sweep until the next daily cycle files a fresh one.

I did **not** file the consolidated canon issue you approved — canon already had it twice ([#1149](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1149), [#1133](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1133)). A third would have been noise, so I added the fleet-wide cost measurement to #1149 instead and cross-linked the four member-repo duplicates.

> ⚠️ Still open: **14 lane-blockers** need you — 6 blocking failure parks ([Shepherd #205](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/issues/205) is a real bug: the fleet sweep can't read its own repo's `.claudinite-settings.json`, 404), 2 torn items no janitor rule can see ([Claudinite #1086](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1086), [ClaudiniteCanary #133](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/133)), and 6 bare `needs-human` that decode to failure. **31 retired-id items** are safe to bulk-close whenever you want. The **R1 loop keeps minting ~53 parks** until #1149 is fixed. **11 repos still carry pre-migration janitor pointers** that will skip one sweep each — say the word and I'll fire the `wake` lever across all of them tonight rather than letting them drift a day.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. - **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.

- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.

content.text:
Full re-sweep done — 14 active repos, six days on from the last scan.

## Headline

**187 open work items, up from 175.** But the shape has changed in an important way: there is **nothing queued and nothing running**. Not one `task:ready` item fleet-wide, and no live `task:agent` claim. The machinery has drained everything it can drain.

**132 of the 187 — 71% — are parked waiting on you.** The fleet isn't stuck; it's blocked on the owner.

## By category

| # | Category | N | Δ since 08-24 | Self-heals? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **R1** — agent lane couldn't converge its own item | **86** | +15 | Lane frees, but mints a new park daily |
| 2 | **R5** — genuine outcome awaiting a human | **46** | +2 | No — this is your real queue |
| 3 | **R4** — retired pack/task id | **30** | −1 | No, but inert. Safe to bulk-close |
| 4 | **R8** — blocked on a dependency | **10** | +1 | Yes, when blockers close |
| 5 | **R9** — bare `needs-human`, live pack | **5** | −1 | No — decodes to failure, holds the lane |
| 6 | **R3** — blocking failure park, live pack | **5** | −1 | No — needs a human |
| 7 | **Mechanically stuck** | **3** | +1 | **No — invisible to every rule** |
| 8 | Owner issues (not work items) | 2 | — | n/a |

## The three genuinely stuck items

This is the only category where the machinery is failing rather than waiting.

- **[Claudinite #1086](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1086)** — torn, untouched since 08-20. **10 days.**
- **[ClaudiniteCanary #133](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/133)** — torn, untouched since 08-19. **11 days.**
- **[Claudinite #1160](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1160)** — **new, and a different failure**: stuck `task:executing` since 08-24 22:17. **5.5 days.**

The two torn items are the known R6 gap, now eleven days old and proven twice over — the fleet-wide wake on 08-24 swept 30 claims around them and left these exactly as they were.

**#1160 is a new finding and the more serious one.** The executing-leash reclaim is documented in `janitor-rules.mjs` as riding the scheduler run to recover a dead executor's item in ~2h. It has not fired in 5.5 days. Worth noting the cron moved from hourly to twice-daily ([#1236](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1236), still blocked and unverified), which would stretch ~2h to ~12h — but not to 132. I haven't root-caused it, so I'm flagging it rather than asserting the cause.

## Two pile-ups worth naming

**ClaudiniteCanary is filing the same failure every single day.** Seven copies of `claudinite-dashboard/fleet-digest`, all `needs-human-action`, one per day: [#157](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/157), [#186](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/186), [#227](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/227), [#241](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/241), [#258](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/258), [#264](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/264), [#269](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/269). Three of those are new since the last scan. One task, failing identically, every day, with nothing stopping it.

**hitbut carries 22 of the 46 R5 items** — nearly half your entire human queue in one repo, and it's largely the same nine tasks filed twice on 08-23 ([#9](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/9)–[#20](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/20) and [#71](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/71)–[#79](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/79)).

## One real improvement, one regression

**WIP went 9 → 1.** Only [#90](https://github.com/missingbulb/WIP/issues/90) remains. Something cleared that backlog properly.

**Shepherd gained a new blocking failure**: [#300](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/issues/300) `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/fleet-usage`, parked 08-27. Notable because [Claudinite #1166](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1166) is an open approval to *retire* that very task — so it's failing while its own removal waits on you.

## What the R1 number means

R1 grew 71 → 86 in six days: **+15, roughly 2.5 new parks a day**, exactly the daily-cycle rate you'd predict. [Canon #1149](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1149) is now responsible for **46% of every open item in the fleet**. Everything else on this list is finite and shrinking; this one compounds.

> ⚠️ Still open: **3 mechanically stuck items** — the 2 torn ([Claudinite #1086](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1086), [Canary #133](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/133), 10–11 days) and the newly-found [Claudinite #1160](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1160) stuck `task:executing` 5.5 days past a leash that should have reclaimed it in ~2h. **10 lane-blockers** (5 R3 + 5 R9). **30 retired-id items** safe to bulk-close. **86 R1 parks** growing ~2.5/day until #1149 lands. Canary's fleet-digest has failed 7 days running with nothing stopping it. I made no changes this pass — read-only, as asked. Say the word for any of: clearing the torn items, diagnosing #1160's dead leash, bulk-closing the 30, or stopping Canary's daily fleet-digest failure.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

content.text:
I've got what I need, and three of your five points need a correction before I build — two rest on premises the evidence contradicts, and one would reverse a deliberate safety ceiling.

**Point 1 — the Canary items aren't a code error, and `action` isn't a mislabel.** [#269's](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/issues/269) worker printed this before exiting non-zero:

```
claudinite-needs-human: action — FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN is not set. Add a repo secret...
```

`code-work.mjs:135` documents that channel deliberately: *"a 403 from a token without the scope it needs is a person's five-second fix, and an exception in its own code is a bug — and the executor, reading an exit code, cannot tell those apart."* The worker knew, said `action`, and `action` is right — a human must add a secret.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

input.title: A parked item survives the fix — nothing closes it when a later run of the same task succeeds
input.body:
A `needs-human` park is a question about a moment: *this run of this task needs a person*. Nothing ever revisits that question. When the cause is later fixed and the task runs clean, the park stays open forever, and a person still has to read it to discover it is already answered.

## The evidence

A 2026-08-30 sweep of all 14 active fleet members found **187 open work items, 132 of them parked on a human**. A large share are parks whose cause is long resolved or long superseded.

The clearest specimens:

- **`missingbulb/hitbut`** carries **22** parked items — nearly half the fleet's entire human queue — and they are the same nine tasks filed twice on 2026-08-23. Every one parked `action` for the same single cause: `the Actions secret CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN ... is not set in this repo`. One missing secret, 22 issues.
- **`missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary`** carries **7** copies of `claudinite-dashboard/fleet-digest`, one per day from 08-22 to 08-27, every one parked `action` on `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN is not set`.
- **[#1086](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1086)** has been parked since 2026-08-20 on a repository-scope blocker that no longer exists.

In each case the moment a run of that task converges clean, every older park on that task is answered — and nothing says so.

## The rule

A janitor rule (this is judgment over history, which is the janitor's stated remit, not the scheduler run's label mechanics): a parked item whose task has since converged `task:status:done` **strictly later** than the park converges `task:status:rejected`, with a comment naming the run that answered it.

Scoped to the two park kinds that name a *broken thing*:

- **`failure`** and **`action`** — these say something is broken or missing. A later clean run is proof it is not broken any more.
- **`approval` and `decision` are excluded**, deliberately. Those parks carry content a person still owes an answer to — an approval park typically holds an open PR (`missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary#133` holds PR #134). Closing one because a later run succeeded would abandon real work.

Strictly-later matters: an equal-or-earlier success says nothing about a failure that came after it.

## What this does not fix

It cleans up *after* a cause is fixed. It does not stop a task re-filing daily *while* the cause persists — that is why Canary reached seven copies, and it is a separate question about how a non-blocking park interacts with standing-item instantiation. Not in scope here.

input.title: adopt-requested-packs should land its PR, not hold it for review
input.body:
`claudinite-lifecycle/adopt-requested-packs` declares `expected_outcome: 'open-pr'`, with the comment *"a new pack switches on checks in this repo's CI — always reviewed, never auto-merged"*.

In practice that ceiling is where fleet pack-adoption stops. `missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary#133` did its work correctly on 2026-08-19 — confirmed `github-actions` as a genuine fit, settled four fingerprints against the checkout, opened PR #134 — and then parked for approval. **Eleven days later the PR is still unmerged and the item is still open.** The adoption never reached the repo it was for.

The owner's call (2026-08-30) is to remove the ceiling: adoptions land unattended.

## Change

`expected_outcome: 'open-pr'` → `'merged-pr'`, and the declaration comment rewritten to state the new posture rather than the old one.

## What this trades away

Stated plainly, because the existing comment is a deliberate decision being reversed: a pack adoption edits the declaration and re-vendors, which switches on that pack's checks in the member's CI. Landing unattended means a member's gate surface can change with no human in front of it. The adoption PR still runs the member's own checks before it merges, so a pack whose checks fail on that repo cannot land — but a pack whose checks *pass* and are merely unwanted now arrives without being asked about.

Refs #1339

input.head: claude/superseded-parks
input.body:
Two independent changes, one commit each, both from a 2026-08-30 sweep of all 14 active fleet members: **187 open work items, 132 of them parked on a human.**

## Janitor rule E — the superseded park

Closes #1452.

A park is a question about a moment. Nothing revisited it, so a fixed cause left the question standing. `missingbulb/hitbut` carries **22** parked items — nearly half the fleet's human queue — all the same nine tasks, all parked `action` on one unset `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN`.

A parked item whose task has since converged `task:status:done` **strictly later** now closes `task:status:rejected`, with a comment naming the run that answered it.

Scoped to `failure` and `action` — the kinds that name a broken thing. **`approval` and `decision` are excluded deliberately**: those carry content a person still owes an answer to, and an approval park typically holds an open PR (`missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary#133` holds PR #134), so closing one would abandon real work.

The rule is pure and knows nothing about how the closed half is read; the worker supplies `doneAfter()`. `listDoneWorkItems` is bounded to two pages of most-recently-updated.

## adopt-requested-packs lands its PR

Closes #1453.

`expected_outcome: 'open-pr'` → `'merged-pr'`. The ceiling existed so a human reviewed a change that switches on new checks in the member's CI — but the review never came: `ClaudiniteCanary#133` opened its PR on 08-19 and sat parked for eleven days while the adoption never reached the repo it was for.

The declaration comment now states the trade rather than the posture it no longer has: a member's gate surface can change with no human in front of it. The member's own checks still gate the merge.

## Verification

- 8 new tests in `test/queue/janitor-rules.test.mjs`, **written first and watched fail** on the missing export, then green.
- Full pack suite: **771 tests, 761 pass, 10 fail** — the identical 10 fail on clean `main` (763/753/10), so none are from this change.
- `check_the_world.mjs`: **0 blocking**, 83 advisory, unchanged in kind from `main`.

## Not in scope

This cleans up *after* a cause is fixed. It does not stop a task re-filing daily *while* the cause persists — that is what took `ClaudiniteCanary` to seven copies of `fleet-digest`, and it is a separate question about how a non-blocking park interacts with standing-item instantiation. Deliberately left alone as the smaller change.

PR [#1454](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1454) is up.

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/
  janitor-rules.mjs — new rule E (supersededItems/supersededComment) plus the
  SUPERSEDABLE_PARKS constant; pure, no I/O.
  read.mjs — listDoneWorkItems, a bounded reader for the closed half of the queue.

packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/task-janitor/
  queue-sweep.mjs — evaluates rule E, closes what it claims, and reports the count
  in the health line; doneRunLookup builds the rule's index from the closed items.

packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/adopt-requested-packs/
  task.mjs — expected_outcome open-pr → merged-pr.
```

## What I built, and what I didn't

**(2) Supersession — built.** A park whose task has since converged `done` *strictly later* now closes `rejected`, naming the run that answered it. Scoped to `failure` and `action`; **`approval` and `decision` deliberately excluded** — those hold content someone still owes an answer to, and an approval park usually holds an open PR. Closing Canary #133 that way would have abandoned PR #134.

**(5) Auto-merge — built as you chose.** The declaration comment now states the trade rather than the old posture.

**Verification:** 8 tests written first and watched fail, then green. Full suite 771/761 — the same 10 failures exist on clean `main` (763/753/10), so none are mine. `check_the_world` 0 blocking.

## Three places the evidence went against the premise

**(1) The Canary items are not a mislabel, and the error was not in the code.** The run did fail, but the worker *deliberately* emitted `claudinite-needs-human: action — FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN is not set`. That channel is a documented feature in `code-work.mjs`: *"a 403 from a token without the scope it needs is a person's five-second fix, and an exception in its own code is a bug — and the executor, reading an exit code, cannot tell those apart."* `action` is the correct kind — a human must add a secret. So I did not relabel them; doing so would have destroyed the "here is your five-second fix" signal fleet-wide.

Your real complaint stands and I've recorded it on #1452: the pile-up comes from the task **re-filing daily while the cause persists**, which is a non-blocking park not occupying the standing slot. That's the duplicate generator, and it's untouched by this PR — per your "smallest change, no design bloat" call.

**(4) #1086 will not be cured yet.** Supersession needs a later *successful* `canon-curation/growth-promote`. The most recent one, [#1413](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1413) on 08-28, converged **`rejected`**, not `done`. #1086 closes the first time a growth-promote actually succeeds — not on the next sweep.

**Canary's 7 won't close either** — no `fleet-digest` run has ever succeeded there. Worth knowing: [#1392](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1392) already retires `fleet-digest` outright, which removes them at the source.

**(3) hitbut is the one that pays off immediately** — set `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN`, and the next clean run of each task closes all 22.

## On the fleet force-update

Holding it. The change isn't in canon yet, so forcing now would push a tree without it and prove nothing. The order is: merge #1454 → force-update the fleet → watch the next janitor sweep close superseded parks. Say **LGTM** and I'll merge and drive that sequence.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#1454](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1454) awaiting your merge — the fleet force-update waits on it, deliberately. Three premise corrections above you should read before merging, especially (1): I did **not** relabel the Canary items, because the `action` verdict is a deliberate worker signal, not a bug. #1086 and Canary's 7 will **not** clear on the first sweep, for the reasons given. The duplicate-re-file generator behind Canary and hitbut is diagnosed but unfixed, recorded on [#1452](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1452). Want me to watch the PR for CI and review events? I haven't subscribed.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

content.text: **Point 2 is already fixed on `main`** — [#1446](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1446) closes an item obsolete when its task isn't carried at HEAD. But it only fires when the **executor picks the item**, and a parked item is never picked again — so Canary's 7 parked `fleet-digest` items can never reach it. That's the real gap. Implementing all three fixes.

A failed run parks failure, and a park for a task that is gone closes

Three corrections from the owner, all against the same pile-ups.

A NON-ZERO EXIT IS A FAILURE. The worker's triage marker used to route the
park, so a worker naming `action` moved a failed run into a non-blocking
lane: the standing slot freed and the task re-filed the next day against a
cause nobody had fixed. That is how ClaudiniteCanary reached seven copies of
one fleet-digest failure and hitbut twenty-two. The park is now `failure`
for every failed run; the worker's verdict was always most useful as the
human-facing instruction, and both its kind and its detail are rendered into
the comment. A run that never STARTED keeps its own lane — the
missingSecrets branch is untouched, because nothing failed there.

A PARK FOR A RETIRED TASK CLOSES. #1446 already closes an item whose task
this repo does not carry at HEAD, but only when the executor PICKS it, and a
parked item is never picked again — so that verdict could not reach the set
that needed it most. Janitor rule F applies it to the parked set. An empty
task set orphans nothing: discovery returning nothing is a broken read, not
every task retiring.

The adopt-requested-packs contract test moves with its decision rather than
being loosened — the pin is right to exist, it was just pinning the old
answer.

Refs #1452, #1453
EOF

## You were right on all three

**(1) A non-zero exit is a failure.** I conceded this and implemented it. The marker no longer routes the park — every failed run parks `failure`. And the mechanical consequence is the one that matters: `failure` is lane-blocking, so **this is the root-cause fix for the duplicate piles**, not just a relabel. A worker naming `action` was freeing the standing slot, which is precisely how Canary reached 7 and hitbut 22.

The worker's verdict isn't lost — both its kind and detail now render into the comment (`The worker asks for: **action**` plus the full fix instructions). And I kept one real distinction the test suite already drew: a run that **never started** because a declared secret is unset still parks `action`, because nothing failed there.

**(2) A retired task should stop as obsolete.** [#1446](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1446) already had that verdict — but only on the executor's pick path, and a parked item is never picked again, so it could never reach Canary's 7. Rule F applies it to the parked set. Guarded: an empty task set orphans nothing, since discovery returning nothing is a broken read, not every task retiring.

**(3) CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN was set — and that's now proof the rule works.** hitbut ran `rule-revalidation` [#148](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/148) and `growth-dedup` [#145](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/145) to `done` **today**. Their 08-23 parks are exactly what rule E closes. Checking the history, the parks predate the real fix: hitbut #105 landed the workflow that actually *passes* the secret at 16:18 on 08-23 — the parks are from 11:57 that morning. The secret was set; the workflow wasn't passing it.

## On the CI failure

Two rounds, both my miss, and the same root cause: I verified with `check_the_world.mjs` and a subset of tests. CI also runs **`ci-work-scope.mjs`** (changed-vs-main, which caught the missing pack bumps) and a **broader test glob** including `packs/**/*.test.mjs` (which caught the `open-pr` contract pin in a pack I hadn't touched). I've now run both exactly as CI does — 2694 tests, 0 blocking on both scopes.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.
